easy.def: To promise that you are telling the truth.
examples: I swear I did not eat it.
He swore to tell the truth.
She swears she saw a deer.

more.def: To make a serious promise that you are telling the truth or will do something.
examples: The witness swore to tell the truth.
I swear I will keep your secret.
He swore that he saw lights in the sky.
Do not swear at school.
He swore when he dropped it.
Swearing is not polite.

more.def: To use rude or bad language.
examples: It is rude to swear in front of others.
He swore loudly when he stubbed his toe.
Many schools have a rule against swearing.

easy.def: Water that comes out of your skin when you are hot.
examples: Sweat ran down my face.
Sweat keeps you cool.
He wiped the sweat.

more.def: Salty water that comes out of the skin when you are hot or working hard.
examples: Sweat dripped from the runner's face.
Sweat helps your body cool down.
He wiped the sweat from his forehead.

easy.def: To have water come out of your skin.
examples: I sweat when I run.
He sweated in the sun.
Dogs do not sweat.

more.def: To give off salty water through the skin when you are hot.
examples: I sweat when I run on a hot day.
He sweated in the summer sun.
Runners sweat during a race.
Honey is sweet.
The apple was sweet.
I like sweet cookies.

more.def: Having the taste of sugar or honey.
examples: Ripe strawberries are sweet and juicy.
The tea was too sweet for me.
Maple syrup is a sweet treat made from tree sap.
What a sweet kitten!
You are sweet to help me.
She gave me a sweet smile.
It was sweet of you to share your lunch.
The baby has a sweet smile.
She wrote a sweet note to her teacher.

easy.def: A name for someone you love.
examples: Goodnight, sweetheart.
Thanks, sweetheart.
He called her sweetheart.

more.def: A loving name for someone you care about.
examples: "Time for bed, sweetheart," said Dad.
Grandma calls me sweetheart.
"Thank you, sweetheart; that was kind," said Grandpa.

easy.def: A loving name for a child or someone you like.
examples: Time for bed, sweetie.
Thank you, sweetie.
Come here, sweetie.

more.def: A loving name for a child or someone you care about.
examples: "Time for bed, sweetie," said Dad.
Grandma called me sweetie and gave me a hug.
"Thank you, sweetie," said the neighbor.

easy.def: To move through water using your body.
examples: Fish swim.
I swim in the pool.
We swam in the lake.

more.def: To move through water by using your arms, legs or fins.
examples: Fish swim with their fins.
She learned to swim at the pool.
We swam across the lake.

easy.def: A seat that hangs from ropes.
examples: I love the swing.
Push me on the swing.
The swing goes high.

more.def: A seat that hangs from ropes or chains and moves back and forth.
examples: The kids waited their turn on the swing.
Dad pushed me on the swing.
A rope swing hung from the tree.
The door swings.
I swing on the swing.
The monkey swings.

more.def: To move back and forth or in a curve while hanging.
examples: The monkey swung from branch to branch.
The door swung open in the wind.
She swung the bat and hit the ball.

easy.def: A button that turns something on or off.
examples: Flip the light switch.
The switch is on the wall.
Turn the switch.

more.def: A small control that turns a machine or light on or off.
examples: Flip the switch to turn on the lamp.
The switch on the wall is broken.
He pressed the switch and the fan started.

easy.def: To change from one to another.
examples: Let us switch seats.
She switched hands.
I switched to blue.

more.def: To change from one thing to another.
examples: Let's switch seats so I can see.
She switched hands to hold the bag.
The team switched to a new plan.

easy.def: A weapon with a long, sharp blade.
examples: The knight held a sword.
The sword is sharp.
He drew his sword.

more.def: A weapon with a long metal blade and a handle.
examples: The knight held up his sword.
A sword hung on the castle wall.
Long ago, soldiers fought with swords.
